body:
If sessions are already multi-client and labels are already a global mutable board, then the missing thing is not capability but legibility: who is running, for which project, for which task, in what state, and which one wants me. Every 'wild' idea — agents sharing a session, agents tagging each other, remote attach — reduces to a namespace that a human and a program can both read.

Under that reading, zmux is small on purpose: naming plus labels plus a reader. Anything bigger is a second zmx. This hypothesis is the thing to test against the first real agent workflow; if legibility turns out to be enough, the scope is settled.
title: The product is legibility of a world zmx already shares
